findings.F1: The book's gain is mostly timing, but heavily concentrated. Its mean daily return is 0.0516 %, of which 0.0214 % (41 %) is the market's own rise and 0.0302 % is timing. 2020 alone contributes 0.627 of the 0.748 summed daily contributions (84 %), 2018 is negative (−0.086), and window w12 loses −0.125.
findings.F2: A few trades and one coin carry the profit. Of 197 trades (win rate 73 %, median +5.5 %), the top 5 sum to 1094 of 2668 summed trade percent (41 %). ADA's 14 trades sum to 873 (33 %), while BTC's 20 trades average only +1.6 % and add nothing to the book (contribution 0.000002).
findings.F3: Recomputed on folds B and C, upside breaks out of flat 60-day ranges peak at 10 days, not the plan's 20. The mean unusual move is +9.2 % at 10 days (t 2.00, 58 cases), +5.7 % at 20 days (t 1.32, 39 cases) and −1.7 % at 40 days (19 cases).
findings.F4: The idea's comparison holds. Breaks above the 60-day high in flat coins (ER ≤ 0.3) beat the same breaks in trending coins: at 10 days +9.2 % (t 2.00, 58 cases) against +2.7 % (t 0.58, 31 cases); at 20 days +5.7 % against +2.0 % (t 0.32, 22 cases).
findings.F5: The width of the prior 60-day high-low range as a share of price grades the rise; this width is not the tested compression against 180 days. The 20-day unusual move is +19.4 % in the narrowest tercile, −0.6 % in the middle and −1.6 % in the widest (Spearman −0.36, 39 cases). The book's forecast grades it only weakly (Spearman 0.12, terciles +3.3 %, +5.3 %, +8.6 %), consistent with step 5's failed supporting check (−0.034).
findings.F6: Small breaks follow through more than large ones. By distance of the close above the prior 60-day high, the 20-day unusual move is +13.9 % in the smallest tercile, +5.1 % in the middle and −1.9 % in the largest (Spearman −0.19, 39 cases).

ideas.idea: In a coin whose price has gone nowhere over the past 60 days, a daily close above its prior 60-day high is followed by a further rise over the next 10 days. The narrower the prior 60-day high-low range is as a share of the price, the larger that rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader should join upside breaks out of a quiet two-month range over about ten days, and more so the tighter that range is against the price.
ideas.name: tight-range breakout ten days

ideas.idea: In a coin whose price has gone nowhere over the past 60 days, a daily close above its prior 60-day high is followed by a further rise over the next 20 days. The smaller the distance of that close above the prior high, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader should prefer a modest close just past a quiet range's top over a large jump past it, which tends to give its gain back.
ideas.name: small breaks follow through
